title: Variant Delta Heatmap: Automated Cold-Warm KV Footprint and Pin Suggestor
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Produce an automated experiment and publishing pipeline that measures cold vs warm KV cache footprint and tail-latency deltas across current hardware variants (A100/H100/L40S/MI300). Generate per-variant delta heatmaps, surface the dominant bottlenecks (memory vs kernel vs scheduling), and emit a recommended 'fast-pin' suggestion for the model catalog. The output should be a published performance profile JSON and an interactive Grafana heatmap link. This ticket focuses on experiment orchestration, metric normalization, and the first-pass pin suggestion algorithm; instrumentation and UI integration are follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Automated job runs across the 4 hardware SKUs and completes without manual intervention for a 3-seed sample suite
Normalized heatmap artifacts (PNG + JSON) uploaded to perf-artifacts S3 and linked from the model catalog
Profile JSON published to the onboarding catalog schema with fields: sku, cold_kv_mb, warm_kv_mb, tail_p99_latency_ms, delta_tail_p99_ms, fast_pin_recommendation
Fast-pin suggestion produced in human-readable format (reason, confidence score 0-100, fallback variants) and attached to profile
PR with experiment code + CI integration merged and a smoke dashboard created with sample traces
notes: Motivation: current onboarding outputs list static pin recommendations without exposing the cold->warm transition behavior; many customer regressions come from cold-start KV footprint differences between SKUs

Approach: use our continuous-batching harness to replay a canonical prompt suite at controlled concurrency levels (1, 4, 16 tokens/sec equivalent) and capture KV size histograms + per-token latency stacks
Normalization: metrics must be normalized by sequence length and batching configuration; will use median-of-3 seeds and report p50/p90/p99
Pin heuristic: start with rule-based thresholds (delta_tail_p99 > 20% AND warm_kv_mb > model_pin_threshold) then compute a confidence score based on stability across seeds and variance across SKUs
Trade-offs: running exhaustive permutations across batch sizes is expensive. We will prioritize production-like batch distributions from telemetry and iterate later with ML-based ranking
Open question: whether to include quantization modes (int8/4bit) in this pipeline or keep quantization profiling in a separate pass
implementation_steps: 1) Author experiment orchestrator job (k8s CronJob) that spins up runner pods per SKU and collects traces
2) Add telemetry hooks to collect KV size histograms from runtime (reuse ENG-120524 sensors)
3) Implement normalizer service that ingests traces and emits heatmap JSON
4) Implement fast-pin rule engine and map outputs to catalog profile schema
5) Add CI job to run the experiment with a smoke sample on PRs to prevent regressions
6) Publish artifacts to S3 and wire to onboarding catalog API for consumption by Console

2026-03-05: Normalizer service stubed; confirmed median-of-3 seed approach reduces noise by ~18% in early runs.
2026-03-09: Fast-pin rule engine implemented; produced first set of human-readable recommendations for 3 sample models.
2026-03-10: PR opened for review (link above). Need review from infra and platform (cc @Arjun Patel for CI gating).
risks_mitigations: Risk: Experiment cost will spike if we run full batch-size grid across SKUs. Mitigation: cap experiment to telemetry-derived top-3 batch shapes and run nightly for longer sweeps.
Risk: Metric variance on MI300 due to unstable kernel scheduling. Mitigation: add an extra warmup phase and increase seeds for MI300 runs.
Risk: Catalog schema changes may affect downstream consumers. Mitigation: publish a compatibility shim and a changelog entry in Console release notes.
qa_plan: Unit tests for normalizer and rule engine with synthetic traces
Integration test that runs orchestrator against a single-sku local runner in CI
Manual verification: compare published heatmap to raw traces for 5 models and confirm fast-pin rationale
E2E: smoke job runs in staging, artifacts available on S3, Console picks up profile JSON
